sanskrit: kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhavān pratyakṣadarśivān teṣāṃ caritam icchāmi kathyamānaṃ tvayā dvija
english: You have been a direct witness of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas; I wish to hear their deeds narrated by you, O brahmin.

sanskrit: kathaṃ samabhavad bhedas teṣām akliṣṭakarmaṇām tac ca yuddhaṃ kathaṃ vṛttaṃ bhūtāntakaraṇaṃ mahat
english: How did the split arise between those whose deeds were beyond reproach? And how did that great war come to pass — the war that put an end to so many living beings?

sanskrit: pitāmahānāṃ sarveṣāṃ daivenāviṣṭacetasām kārtsnyenaitat samācakṣva bhagavan kuśalo hy asi
english: Tell me all of this in full, concerning all those forefathers whose minds were possessed by fate, O Blessed One, for you are skilled in such telling.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kṛṣṇadvaipāyanas tadā śaśāsa śiṣyam āsīnaṃ vaiśaṃpāyanam antike
english: Hearing those words, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana then instructed his disciple Vaiśaṃpāyana, who was seated nearby.

sanskrit: kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yathā bhedo 'bhavat purā tad asmai sarvam ācakṣva yan mattaḥ śrutavān asi
english: Narrate to him in full how the split between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas came about in former times — everything that you have heard from me.

sanskrit: guror vacanam ājñāya sa tu viprarṣabhas tadā ācacakṣe tataḥ sarvam itihāsaṃ purātanam
english: That bull among brahmins, having received the command of his guru, then narrated the entire ancient history.

sanskrit: tasmai rājñe sadasyebhyaḥ kṣatriyebhyaś ca sarvaśaḥ bhedaṃ rājyavināśaṃ ca kurupāṇḍavayos tadā
english: To that king, to the members of the assembly, and to all the kshatriyas gathered there, he then told the story of the rift and the destruction of the kingdom of the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gurave prāṅ namaskṛtya manobuddhisamādhibhiḥ saṃpūjya ca dvijān sarvāṃs tathānyān viduṣo janān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana spoke: Having first bowed to my guru with mind, intellect, and concentrated thought, and having honoured all the brahmins and other learned persons present —

sanskrit: maharṣeḥ sarvalokeṣu viśrutasyāsya dhīmataḥ pravakṣyāmi mataṃ kṛtsnaṃ vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: — I shall now set forth in full the teaching of Vyāsa, the great sage renowned throughout all the worlds, the wise one of immeasurable splendour.

sanskrit: śrotuṃ pātraṃ ca rājaṃs tvaṃ prāpyemāṃ bhāratīṃ kathām guror vaktuṃ parispando mudā protsāhatīva mām
english: O king, you are a worthy vessel to hear this Bhārata tale; the eagerness to speak on behalf of my guru urges me on with joy, as it were.

sanskrit: śṛṇu rājan yathā bhedaḥ kurupāṇḍavayor abhūt rājyārthe dyūtasaṃbhūto vanavāsas tathaiva ca
english: Hear, O king, how the rift between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas came about: the exile arising from the dice game over the kingdom, and all that followed.

sanskrit: yathā ca yuddham abhavat pṛthivīkṣayakārakam tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi pṛcchate bharatarṣabha
english: And how the war came about — the war that laid waste to the earth — all of that I shall recount to you who ask, O bull of the Bhārata line.

sanskrit: mṛte pitari te vīrā vanād etya svamandiram nacirād iva vidvāṃso vede dhanuṣi cābhavan
english: When their father had died, those heroes returned from the forest to their own dwelling, and in no great time became learned in both the Veda and the bow.

sanskrit: tāṃs tathā rūpavīryaujaḥsaṃpannān paurasaṃmatān nāmṛṣyan kuravo dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavāñ śrīyaśobhṛtaḥ
english: Seeing the Pāṇḍavas endowed with beauty, valour, and vigour, approved of by the citizens, and bearing glory and renown, the Kurus could not endure them.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ krūraḥ karṇaś ca sahasaubalaḥ teṣāṃ nigrahanirvāsān vividhāṃs te samācaran
english: Then the cruel Duryodhana, together with Karṇa and Śakuni son of Subala, undertook various schemes to suppress and banish them.

sanskrit: dadāv atha viṣaṃ pāpo bhīmāya dhṛtarāṣṭrajaḥ jarayām āsa tad vīraḥ sahānnena vṛkodaraḥ
english: That wicked son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra then administered poison to Bhīma; but the hero Vṛkodara digested it along with his food.

sanskrit: pramāṇakoṭyāṃ saṃsuptaṃ punar baddhvā vṛkodaram toyeṣu bhīmaṃ gaṅgāyāḥ prakṣipya puram āvrajat
english: Then, binding the sleeping Vṛkodara at Pramanakoți and hurling Bhīma into the waters of the Gaṅgā, he returned to the city.

sanskrit: yadā prabuddhaḥ kaunteyas tadā saṃchidya bandhanam udatiṣṭhan mahārāja bhīmaseno gatavyathaḥ
english: When Kaunteya awoke, he snapped his bonds and arose, O great king — Bhīmasena, free of all distress.

sanskrit: āśīviṣaiḥ kṛṣṇasarpaiḥ suptaṃ cainam adaṃśayat sarveṣv evāṅgadeśeṣu na mamāra ca śatruhā
english: He also had him bitten all over his body by venomous black serpents while he slept; yet that slayer of foes did not die.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu viprakāreṣu teṣu teṣu mahāmatiḥ mokṣaṇe pratighāte ca viduro 'vahito 'bhavat
english: In each and every one of those acts of harm, the great-minded Vidura was ever watchful in rescuing and countering them.

sanskrit: svargastho jīvalokasya yathā śakraḥ sukhāvahaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ tathā nityaṃ viduro 'pi sukhāvahaḥ
english: Just as Indra, dwelling in heaven, ever brings welfare to the living world, so too did Vidura ever bring welfare to the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yadā tu vividhopāyaiḥ saṃvṛtair vivṛtair api nāśaknod vinihantuṃ tān daivabhāvyartharakṣitān
english: But when, despite all manner of concealed and open stratagems, he could not kill those who were protected by fate and divine will —

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃmantrya sacivair vṛṣaduḥśāsanādibhiḥ dhṛtarāṣṭram anujñāpya jātuṣaṃ gṛham ādiśat
english: — then, having taken counsel with his ministers headed by Vrisha and Duḥśāsana, and having obtained Dhṛtarāṣṭra's permission, he ordered the house of lac.

sanskrit: tatra tān vāsayām āsa pāṇḍavān amitaujasaḥ adāhayac ca visrabdhān pāvakena punas tadā
english: He had the Pāṇḍavas of boundless might housed there, and then, when they were off guard, he set fire to them with a conflagration.

sanskrit: vidurasyaiva vacanāt khanitrī vihitā tataḥ mokṣayām āsa yogena te muktāḥ prādravan bhayāt
english: But by Vidura's counsel a tunnel had been prepared beforehand; by this means he delivered them, and they, freed, fled in fear.

sanskrit: tato mahāvane ghore hiḍimbaṃ nāma rākṣasam bhīmaseno 'vadhīt kruddho bhuvi bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: Then in the dreadful great forest, Bhīmasena of fearsome might, enraged, slew on the earth the rakshasa named Hiḍimba.

sanskrit: atha saṃdhāya te vīrā ekacakrāṃ vrajaṃs tadā brahmarūpadharā bhūtvā mātrā saha paraṃtapāḥ
english: Then those heroes, scorchers of foes, having set out together for the city of Ekacakra, went there in the guise of brahmins, accompanied by their mother.

sanskrit: tatra te brāhmaṇārthāya bakaṃ hatvā mahābalam brāhmaṇaiḥ sahitā jagmuḥ pāñcālānāṃ puraṃ tataḥ
english: There, for the sake of a brahmin, they slew the mighty Baka, and then, in the company of brahmins, they departed for the city of the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: te tatra draupadīṃ labdhvā parisaṃvatsaroṣitāḥ viditā hāstinapuraṃ pratyājagmur ariṃdamāḥ
english: There, having won Draupadī and resided for the full period of a year, those tamers of enemies returned to Hāstinapura, now known for who they were.

sanskrit: ta uktā dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rājñā śāṃtanavena ca bhrātṛbhir vigrahas tāta kathaṃ vo na bhaved iti asmābhiḥ khāṇḍavaprasthe yuṣmadvāso 'nucintitaḥ
english: They were addressed by King Dhṛtarāṣṭra son of Śaṃtanu: "My dear sons, why should there be conflict between you and your brothers? We have thought of a dwelling for you at Khāṇḍavaprastha."

sanskrit: tasmāj janapadopetaṃ suvibhaktamahāpatham vāsāya khāṇḍavaprasthaṃ vrajadhvaṃ gatamanyavaḥ
english: "Therefore, setting aside your anger, go to Khāṇḍavaprastha to dwell there — a land endowed with populated territories and well-laid broad roads."

sanskrit: tayos te vacanāj jagmuḥ saha sarvaiḥ suhṛjjanaiḥ nagaraṃ khāṇḍavaprasthaṃ ratnāny ādāya sarvaśaḥ
english: At the word of those two, they departed, taking all manner of gems and jewels, along with all their friends and well-wishers, for the city of Khāṇḍavaprastha.

sanskrit: tatra te nyavasan rājan saṃvatsaragaṇān bahūn vaśe śastrapratāpena kurvanto 'nyān mahīkṣitaḥ
english: There they dwelt, O king, for many years, bringing other kings under their dominion by the might of their arms.

sanskrit: evaṃ dharmapradhānās te satyavrataparāyaṇāḥ apramattotthitāḥ kṣāntāḥ pratapanto 'hitāṃs tadā
english: Ever foremost in dharma, devoted to vows of truth, alert and diligent, forbearing, yet blazing with power against their enemies — such were they in those days.

sanskrit: ajayad bhīmasenas tu diśaṃ prācīṃ mahābalaḥ udīcīm arjuno vīraḥ pratīcīṃ nakulas tathā
english: The mighty Bhīmasena conquered the eastern quarter; the heroic Arjuna, the northern; and Nakula likewise conquered the western.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāṃ sahadevas tu vijigye paravīrahā evaṃ cakrur imāṃ sarve vaśe kṛtsnāṃ vasuṃdharām
english: Sahadeva, slayer of enemy heroes, conquered the southern quarter; and together they brought the entire earth under their sway.

sanskrit: pañcabhiḥ sūryasaṃkāśaiḥ sūryeṇa ca virājatā ṣaṭsūryevābabhau pṛthvī pāṇḍavaiḥ satyavikramaiḥ
english: With five Pāṇḍavas resplendent as the sun, and with the sun itself blazing, the earth shone as if lit by six suns — the Pāṇḍavas of true valour.

sanskrit: tato nimitte kasmiṃś cid dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vanaṃ prasthāpayām āsa bhrātaraṃ vai dhanaṃjayam
english: Then, on account of a certain circumstance, King Yudhiṣṭhira the Dharmarāja sent his brother Dhanañjaya to the forest.

sanskrit: sa vai saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ māsaṃ caikaṃ vane 'vasat tato 'gacchad dhṛṣīkeśaṃ dvāravatyāṃ kadā cana
english: He dwelt in the forest for a full year and one month, and then at some point went to Hṛṣīkeśa at Dvāravatī.

sanskrit: labdhavāṃs tatra bībhatsur bhāryāṃ rājīvalocanām anujāṃ vāsudevasya subhadrāṃ bhadrabhāṣiṇīm
english: There Bībhatsu obtained as wife the lotus-eyed Subhadrā, the younger sister of Vāsudeva, she of auspicious speech.

sanskrit: sā śacīva mahendreṇa śrīḥ kṛṣṇeneva saṃgatā subhadrā yuyuje prītā pāṇḍavenārjunena ha
english: Subhadrā, delighted, was united with the Pāṇḍava Arjuna just as Śacī is with great Indra, or as Śrī is united with Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: atarpayac ca kaunteyaḥ khāṇḍave havyavāhanam bībhatsur vāsudevena sahito nṛpasattama
english: And Bībhatsu, that Kaunteya, together with Vāsudeva, satisfied the fire — the carrier of oblations — in the Khāṇḍava forest, O best of kings.

sanskrit: nātibhāro hi pārthasya keśavenābhavat saha vyavasāyasahāyasya viṣṇoḥ śatruvadheṣv iva
english: For Pārtha, with Keśava as companion in his endeavours, bore no excessive burden — even as Viṣṇu is with his allies in the slaying of foes.

sanskrit: pārthāyāgnir dadau cāpi gāṇḍīvaṃ dhanur uttamam iṣudhī cākṣayair bāṇai rathaṃ ca kapilakṣaṇam
english: Agni also gave to Pārtha the supreme bow Gāṇḍīva, two inexhaustible quivers with arrows, and a chariot marked with the monkey-banner.

sanskrit: mokṣayām āsa bībhatsur mayaṃ tatra mahāsuram sa cakāra sabhāṃ divyāṃ sarvaratnasamācitām
english: Bībhatsu rescued there the great asura Maya, and he in turn fashioned a divine assembly hall filled with every kind of gem.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ duryodhano mando lobhaṃ cakre sudurmatiḥ tato 'kṣair vañcayitvā ca saubalena yudhiṣṭhiram
english: In that hall, the dull-witted and most evil-minded Duryodhana conceived his covetousness; and thereafter, with Śakuni son of Subala, he cheated Yudhiṣṭhira at dice.

sanskrit: vanaṃ prasthāpayām āsa sapta varṣāṇi pañca ca ajñātam ekaṃ rāṣṭre ca tathā varṣaṃ trayodaśam
english: He sent them to the forest for twelve years, and for the thirteenth year to live unrecognized within the kingdom — thus thirteen years in all.

sanskrit: tataś caturdaśe varṣe yācamānāḥ svakaṃ vasu nālabhanta mahārāja tato yuddham avartata
english: Then in the fourteenth year, when they sought their rightful property, they did not obtain it, O great king, and so the war began.

sanskrit: tatas te sarvam utsādya hatvā duryodhanaṃ nṛpam rājyaṃ vidrutabhūyiṣṭhaṃ pratyapadyanta pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Having then destroyed everything and slain King Duryodhana, the Pāṇḍavas recovered the kingdom, now emptied of most of its people.

sanskrit: evam etat purāvṛttaṃ teṣām akliṣṭakarmaṇām bhedo rājyavināśaś ca jayaś ca jayatāṃ vara
english: Such was the ancient story of those whose deeds were beyond reproach: the rift, the destruction of the kingdom, and the victory — O best of conquerors.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathitaṃ vai samāsena tvayā sarvaṃ dvijottama mahābhāratam ākhyānaṃ kurūṇāṃ caritaṃ mahat
english: Janamejaya spoke: You have narrated in summary, O best of brahmins, the entire Mahābhārata — the great story of the deeds of the Kurus.

sanskrit: kathāṃ tv anagha citrārthām imāṃ kathayati tvayi vistaraśravaṇe jātaṃ kautūhalam atīva me
english: But as you narrate this tale of wondrous import, O sinless one, an exceeding great curiosity has arisen in me to hear it at length.

sanskrit: sa bhavān vistareṇemāṃ punar ākhyātum arhati na hi tṛpyāmi pūrveṣāṃ śṛṇvānaś caritaṃ mahat
english: You, sir, should narrate this again in full detail; for I am not satisfied, listening to the great deeds of the ancestors.

sanskrit: na tat kāraṇam alpaṃ hi dharmajñā yatra pāṇḍavāḥ avadhyān sarvaśo jaghnuḥ praśasyante ca mānavaiḥ
english: For the cause cannot have been trivial — those who know dharma, the Pāṇḍavas, killed men who were in principle inviolable, and yet they are praised by all people.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ te naravyāghrāḥ śaktāḥ santo hy anāgasaḥ prayujyamānān saṃkleśān kṣāntavanto durātmanām
english: For what reason did those tigers among men, though capable and themselves without fault, endure the afflictions inflicted upon them by the wicked?

sanskrit: kathaṃ nāgāyutaprāṇo bāhuśālī vṛkodaraḥ parikliśyann api krodhaṃ dhṛtavān vai dvijottama
english: How was it that Vṛkodara, mighty of arm, with the strength of ten thousand elephants, could restrain his anger even while suffering great torment, O best of brahmins?

sanskrit: kathaṃ sā draupadī kṛṣṇā kliśyamānā durātmabhiḥ śaktā satī dhārtarāṣṭrān nādahad ghoracakṣuṣā
english: How was it that Draupadī the dark one, being tormented by the wicked, chaste as she was and possessed of terrible eyes, did not burn the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra?

sanskrit: kathaṃ vyatikraman dyūte pārthau mādrīsutau tathā anuvrajan naravyāghraṃ vañcyamānaṃ durātmabhiḥ
english: How did the two Pārthas and the two sons of Mādrī, passing over the transgression at the dice game, follow that tiger among men even as he was being cheated by the wicked?

sanskrit: kathaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ suto dharmasya dharmavit anarhaḥ paramaṃ kleśaṃ soḍhavān sa yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: How was it that Yudhiṣṭhira, the foremost of those who uphold dharma, the son of Dharma himself, a knower of dharma, who deserved no such thing, could endure the utmost affliction?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca bahulāḥ senāḥ pāṇḍavaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ asyann eko 'nayat sarvāḥ pitṛlokaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: And how did Dhanañjaya, the Pāṇḍava with Kṛṣṇa as his charioteer, single-handedly shooting arrows, send all those vast armies to the world of the fathers?

sanskrit: etad ācakṣva me sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ tapodhana yad yac ca kṛtavantas te tatra tatra mahārathāḥ
english: Tell me all of this as it truly occurred, O wealth of asceticism, and whatever those great chariot-warriors did on each occasion.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca maharṣeḥ sarvalokeṣu pūjitasya mahātmanaḥ pravakṣyāmi mataṃ kṛtsnaṃ vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana spoke: I shall now set forth in full the teaching of Vyāsa, the great sage of great soul worshipped throughout all the worlds, the one of immeasurable splendour.

sanskrit: idaṃ śatasahasraṃ hi ślokānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām satyavatyātmajeneha vyākhyātam amitaujasā
english: For this collection of a hundred thousand verses of meritorious deeds has been expounded here by the son of Satyavatī, that one of boundless might.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ śrāvayed vidvān yaś cedaṃ śṛṇuyān naraḥ te brahmaṇaḥ sthānam etya prāpnuyur devatulyatām
english: The learned man who has this recited, and the person who hears it — they, having attained the abode of Brahman, shall reach a state equal to that of the gods.

sanskrit: idaṃ hi vedaiḥ samitaṃ pavitram api cottamam śrāvyāṇām uttamaṃ cedaṃ purāṇam ṛṣisaṃstutam
english: This is equal to the Vedas, most sacred, most excellent; this Purāṇa is the foremost of all things worth hearing, and it is praised by the seers.

sanskrit: asminn arthaś ca dharmaś ca nikhilenopadiśyate itihāse mahāpuṇye buddhiś ca parinaiṣṭhikī
english: In this most meritorious history, artha, dharma, and ultimate wisdom are taught in their entirety.

sanskrit: akṣudrān dānaśīlāṃś ca satyaśīlān anāstikān kārṣṇaṃ vedam imaṃ vidvāñ śrāvayitvārtham aśnute
english: One who, knowing this Veda of Kṛṣṇa, has it recited to those who are not petty-minded, who are given to charity, devoted to truth, and not unbelievers, shall attain the highest good.

sanskrit: bhrūṇahatyākṛtaṃ cāpi pāpaṃ jahyād asaṃśayam itihāsam imaṃ śrutvā puruṣo 'pi sudāruṇaḥ
english: Even the sin incurred by the killing of an embryo is undoubtedly shed — even a most hardened man, upon hearing this history.

sanskrit: jayo nāmetihāso 'yaṃ śrotavyo vijigīṣuṇā mahīṃ vijayate sarvāṃ śatrūṃś cāpi parājayet
english: This history named Jaya should be heard by one who desires victory; he shall conquer the entire earth and vanquish his enemies as well.

sanskrit: idaṃ puṃsavanaṃ śreṣṭham idaṃ svastyayanaṃ mahat mahiṣīyuvarājābhyāṃ śrotavyaṃ bahuśas tathā
english: This is the best rite for obtaining a male child; this is a great rite of blessing; it should be heard many times by the queen and the crown prince alike.

sanskrit: arthaśāstram idaṃ puṇyaṃ dharmaśāstram idaṃ param mokṣaśāstram idaṃ proktaṃ vyāsenāmitabuddhinā
english: This is a sacred treatise on wealth; this is the supreme treatise on dharma; this is declared to be the treatise on liberation, by Vyāsa of boundless intellect.

sanskrit: saṃpraty ācakṣate caiva ākhyāsyanti tathāpare putrāḥ śuśrūṣavaḥ santi preṣyāś ca priyakāriṇaḥ
english: Some relate it even now; others will relate it hereafter; there are sons who are eager to serve, and attendants who do whatever is pleasing.

sanskrit: śarīreṇa kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vācā ca manasaiva ca sarvaṃ tat tyajati kṣipram idaṃ śṛṇvan naraḥ sadā
english: All the sin committed by body, by speech, and by mind — a person who always hears this swiftly sheds all of it.

sanskrit: bhāratānāṃ mahaj janma śṛṇvatām anasūyatām nāsti vyādhibhayaṃ teṣāṃ paralokabhayaṃ kutaḥ
english: Those who listen without envy to the great birth-narrative of the Bhāratas shall have no fear of disease — how then could they fear the world beyond?

sanskrit: dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ puṇyaṃ tathaiva ca kṛṣṇadvaipāyanenedaṃ kṛtaṃ puṇyacikīrṣuṇā
english: This, which confers prosperity, renown, long life, heaven, and merit, was composed by Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, who desired to bestow merit.

sanskrit: kīrtiṃ prathayatā loke pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām anyeṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca bhūridraviṇatejasām
english: He composed it to spread the fame throughout the world of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, and of the other kshatriyas of abundant wealth and splendour.

sanskrit: yathā samudro bhagavān yathā ca himavān giriḥ khyātāv ubhau ratnanidhī tathā bhāratam ucyate
english: Just as the blessed ocean and the mountain Himavat are both renowned as treasuries of gems, so the Bhārata is called a treasury of gems.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ śrāvayed vidvān brāhmaṇān iha parvasu dhūtapāpmā jitasvargo brahmabhūyaṃ sa gacchati
english: The learned man who has this recited to brahmins here on the occasion of the parvan days — his sins shaken off, heaven won — he attains the state of Brahman.

sanskrit: yaś cedaṃ śrāvayec chrāddhe brāhmaṇān pādam antataḥ akṣayyaṃ tasya tac chrāddham upatiṣṭhet pitṝn api
english: And one who has even a single verse of this recited to brahmins at a shraddha ceremony — that shraddha of his shall remain inexhaustible, and shall fully reach his ancestors.

sanskrit: ahnā yad enaś cājñānāt prakaroti naraś caran tan mahābhāratākhyānaṃ śrutvaiva pravilīyate
english: Whatever sin a person commits unknowingly in the course of a day — all of that dissolves simply upon hearing this narrative called the Mahābhārata.
